subject: Private runtime exit channels and firewall enforcement review
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Dan Morris <dan.morris@acmehealth.com>, security@acmehealth.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private runtime exit channels and firewall enforcement review

Dan / ACME security team —

Thanks for the intake form and the firewall snapshot (attached). We want to make sure the private deployment we're standing up at ACME (private runtime + customer-managed control plane egress) meets your outbound requirements. A few concrete asks so we can produce a concise allowlist and enforcement proposal: 

- Can you confirm which of the attached CIDR blocks in acme_firewall_config_v1.pdf are the dedicated outbound ranges you will permit for a third-party control plane? If you have per-environment distinctions (prod/stage), please note them.
- Which TCP/UDP ports will you explicitly allow for control plane callbacks and health checks? (examples below)
- Do you require mTLS for control plane connections? If yes, are there client cert rotation constraints or CA pinning we should be aware of?
- Do you expect hostname/SNI validation (e.g., control.redwood-inference.com) vs raw IP-based filtering?
- Any DNS egress constraints — must DNS queries go to an internal resolver only?
- Audit/logging requirements for connection attempts (e.g., flow logs retained 90 days, syslog ship to Splunk)

To speed this, I attached our recommended minimal outbound footprint (connection_matrix.csv) — it maps logical flows to ports and TLS expectations. Once we have the answers above we will produce a single-page firewall rule statement for ACME's network team and a short runbook for on-call ops.

Next steps: If useful, we can schedule a 30-minute tech review with network ops.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com

Attachments: acme_firewall_config_v1.pdf (attachment), connection_matrix.csv (attachment)

From: Dan Morris <dan.morris@acmehealth.com>

Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 12:20:00 -0700

On Wed, Mar 3, 2027 at 9:12 AM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Dan / ACME security team —
> 
> Thanks for the intake form and the firewall snapshot (attached). We want to make sure the private deployment we're standing up at ACME (private runtime + customer-managed control plane egress) meets your outbound requirements. A few concrete asks so we can produce a concise allowlist and enforcement proposal: 
> 
> - Can you confirm which of the attached CIDR blocks in acme_firewall_config_v1.pdf are the dedicated outbound ranges you will permit for a third-party control plane? If you have per-environment distinctions (prod/stage), please note them.

Thanks, Olga — sorry for the short reply, here's the immediate config constraints from our network team (see connection_matrix.csv for mapping):

- Allowed egress: only to the following public IPs (we gate via NAT): 34.82.191.12, 35.199.44.77, 34.102.183.9. These are the only public endpoints we will permit outbound to third-party control planes.
- Ports required: 443 (HTTPS/TLS) for API/control callbacks; 5222 is not permitted; 80 is blocked.
- TLS: mTLS is preferred for sensitive control plane actions but we can accept TLS 1.2+ with strict SNI check if you cannot do mTLS immediately. SNI must match control.acme.redwood.com.
- DNS: outbound DNS must be to our internal resolver only (10.10.0.2); no recursive queries to public resolvers allowed.
- Session timeouts: idle TCP sessions may be torn down after 5 minutes; keepalives are recommended.
- Audit: we require connection-level logs retained 180 days and a daily summary delivered to our security mailbox (security@acmehealth.com).

Attached: connection_matrix.csv (CSV) — includes the mapping of logical service names to allowed IPs/ports and recommended timeouts.

If you can provide a proposed allowlist statement and minimum TLS/cert profile, we will fast-track it with network ops.

—Dan
Dan Morris
Infrastructure Lead, ACME Health
dan.morris@acmehealth.com

Attachments: connection_matrix.csv (attachment)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private runtime exit channels and firewall enforcement review

Forwarding Dan's response — key constraints: only three allowed public IPs (34.82.191.12, 35.199.44.77, 34.102.183.9), TLS + SNI required, DNS to internal resolver, 5-minute idle teardown, 180-day log retention.

Questions for Rishi: can our private control plane (customer-managed deployment) present a stable client IP that matches those three IPs, or do we need ACME to accept a short-lived egress pool? If the latter, we'll need to propose a proxy/NAT option. Also: can we meet mTLS quickly or do we propose strict SNI+certificate pinning as interim?

Laura — recommend we prepare the single-page allowlist doc and an ops runbook for connection failures and log evidence. Vanessa — please confirm who on CS should be the ACME contact for the daily summary delivery and whether we should expect a dedicated Splunk endpoint or mailbox.

I'll draft the allowlist once we have answers.

Thanks,
Olga

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private runtime exit channels and firewall enforcement review

Thanks — good catch, team. Proposed approach below so we can send this to ACME as the official statement and runbook excerpt.

1) Allowlist statement (single page) — what we'll ask ACME to apply to their perimeter firewall: 
   - Source: customer nodes (this is ACME's firewall) will permit outbound TCP 443 to the following destination IPs: 34.82.191.12, 35.199.44.77, 34.102.183.9 (single-entry per line).
   - Destination TLS: control.acme.redwood.com must be presented as SNI. TLS 1.2+ required.
   - Auth: mTLS for administrative/control operations. For initial connectivity we will accept TLS with strict certificate validation (certificate pinned to Redwood's current CA) while mTLS rollout completes.
   - DNS: Allow outbound DNS only to 10.10.0.2; Redwood will not perform recursive DNS queries to public resolvers; all hostnames will resolve to the allowed IPs above prior to connection.
   - Session behavior: implement TCP idle timeout >= 6 minutes or allow keepalives; retry/backoff policy documented in runbook.
   - Logging: flow logs + TLS metadata retained 180 days; daily summary to security@acmehealth.com.

2) Ops runbook excerpt (what we will hand to on-call):
   - Failure modes and evidence to collect: TLS handshake failure (capture SNI and certificate chain), IP mismatch, DNS lookup failures (query/response), and NAT translation anomalies.
   - Remediation steps: confirm DNS resolution to allowed IPs, confirm client cert validity (if mTLS), check NAT mapping on ACME side, request connection traces from Redwood's control plane (we will provide trace IDs).
   - Escalation path: ACME security (security@acmehealth.com) -> Redwood CS oncall (cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com) -> Engineering oncall (rishi).

3) Implementation timeline & next steps:
   - Rishi: confirm whether we can provide static egress IPs from our private control plane image or we need to propose an outbound proxy for ACME to trust.
   - Olga: draft the single-page allowlist doc for ACME sign-off (I can review).
   - Vanessa: confirm delivery method for daily summaries and whether a Splunk HTTP endpoint is available.

I'll draft and share the allowlist doc by EOD tomorrow once Rishi confirms the egress option.

Laura Bennett
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Attachments: none
